title: Private deploy: Network compatibility acceleration & legacy host support playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customer requests for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments are increasingly blocked by heterogeneous network environments and legacy host constraints (older OS/kernel, restricted egress, intermittent bastion windows). Current triage is high-touch and inconsistent across SEs, resulting in long lead times and missed SLAs for enterprise customers.

Goal: Produce a compact, operational playbook and a prioritized scoring rubric that SEs and PMRs can apply during intake to: 1) accelerate low-risk customers into a self-serve fast path, 2) surface non-starter compatibility issues early, and 3) create clear remediation lanes for medium/high-risk requests. This playbook should integrate with our existing intake form and produce a deterministic 'lane recommendation' (FastTrack / Concierge / Engineering-Assist / Deferred).

Scope: Networking (egress, proxy, NAT, MTU, DNS), upgrade constraints (patch windows, kernel compatibility, package manager availability), air-gapped topologies (artifact transfer options), and legacy host support (RHEL6/RHEL7, older Windows Server variants, CentOS variants). Excludes full on-prem installation runbooks (handled by Delivery team) but includes pre-flight checks and signalization to Delivery/Eng teams.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric published in Confluence with clear thresholds for FastTrack vs Concierge
Intake form augmented to auto-suggest remediation steps and expected timeline
Runbook checklist (network probes, agent compatibility matrix) created and validated with Solutions Engineering on 3 pilot customers
Escalation matrix documented with SLAs for Engineering-Assist lane and named owners
Two pilot onboardings completed within target time windows and retrospective notes captured
comments: 2025-02-27 - Asha Patel: Drafted scope and initial scoring factors after review with SE lead (Nadia Morales). Key variables: egress ports, bastion-only egress windows, allowed outbound domains, kernel version, package manager offline availability.

2025-02-28 - Liam Chen: Met with Eng runtime team (ENG-22011 owner) to validate feasibility of minimal agent footprint for older kernels. Eng notes: older kernels require backported libssl work; this increases Engineering-Assist effort estimate from 3d -> 10d for those hosts.

2025-03-03 - Asha Patel: Added legacy OS compatibility matrix and sample remediation scripts to Confluence. Flagged two customers where FastTrack is still possible if they enable an ephemeral proxy for artifact download.

2025-03-04 - Solutions Engineering (Nadia Morales): Ran probe on pilot customer ACME-Global; results: MTU mismatch and internal DNS using split-horizon; recommended temporary CNAME and MTU adjustment. Scheduling remediation with customer for 2025-03-10 maintenance window.

2025-03-05 - Liam Chen: Confirmed runbook links and escalations. Created Engineering intake card template for ENG-28490 to track backports and kernel patches required for RHEL7 hosts. Next: finalize Confluence playbook and update intake form to include automated lane selector.
